title: Jordan's $18,000 Is Quietly Shrinking

scenes.say: Jordan's $18,000 earns $0 in checking, and loses about $540 of buying power a year.
He's 31, and that money has sat there for three years, just in case.
His bills are about $3,000 a month, so three months is $9,000.
In a savings account paying around 4%, that half earns about $360 a year.
The other $9,000, he won't need for ten years.
If a broad index fund earned roughly 7% a year, not guaranteed, it could reach about $17,700.
His plan: keep three months safe, set a date to invest the rest, and check once a year.
How much sits in your checking? Subscribe, so your savings aren't $18,000 earning $0.

question: How much of your savings is sitting in checking?
description: Jordan, 31, keeps $18,000 in checking at 0%. With inflation around 3%, it loses roughly $540 of buying power a year. Keeping $9,000 as an emergency fund at around 4% and investing the rest long-term could look very different in 10 years — if markets returned roughly 7%, which is not guaranteed. Rounded US estimates; general education only.
